Begin the repetition: extend your arms out to the sides, keeping them slightly bent at the elbows, and squeeze your shoulder blades together as if you're trying to hold a pencil between them.
Complete the repetition: hold this position for a moment, then gradually lower your arms back down to the setup position.
Continue with control: continue the same controlled motion for the planned repetitions, ensuring to maintain the bend in your knees and keeping your back straight for the full movement.
tp: Setup: Choose a clear, stable surface and establish a balanced position before starting Bodyweight Bent Over Rear Delt Fly.
Control: Keep the motion smooth and let the intended muscles do the work; reduce the resistance if you need momentum to finish a repetition.

n: Twin handle parallel grip lat pulldown (Cable)
st: Set up for the movement: sit on the seat, ensuring your feet are flat on the floor and your knees are under the pads. Reach up and take a firm grip on the twin handles with a neutral grip (palms facing each other).
Begin the repetition: pull the handles down to your chest level while keeping your back straight and your chest lifted. Ensure your elbows are pointing down and slightly forward.
Complete the repetition: hold for a moment at the bottom of the movement, squeezing your shoulder blades together to engage your lat muscles.
Continue with control: gradually release the handles back to the setup position, allowing your arms to fully extend and your lat muscles to stretch. Repeat this process for your planned repetitions.

st: Set up for the movement: begin the movement by swinging your body forward and back in a controlled manner, using your hips and core to generate momentum, which is the "kipping" part of the exercise.

Begin the repetition: push your body up by straightening your arms and lifting your hips off the bench. This is your setup position.
Complete the repetition: lower your body by bending your elbows until your upper arms are about parallel with the floor, keeping your back close to the bench.
Continue with control: push your body back up to the setup position by straightening your arms, squeezing your triceps at the top. This completes one rep.
Continue with control: repeat for the planned number of repetitions, stopping if your form begins to change.
tp: Setup: Choose a clear, stable surface and establish a balanced position before starting Bench Dip with legs on bench.
Control: Keep the motion smooth and let the triceps brachii do the work; reduce the resistance if you need momentum to finish a repetition.
Range and alignment: Use only the range you can control while keeping the working joints aligned. Stop if you feel sharp pain or unusual joint discomfort.
Breathing: Exhale during the effort, inhale during the easier phase, and avoid holding your breath for the entire repetition.
in: The Bench Dip with legs on bench exercise uses this equipment: body weight. It primarily trains Triceps Brachii. It also involves Deltoid Anterior, Latissimus Dorsi, Levator Scapulae, Pectoralis Major Clavicular Head, Pectoralis Major Sternal Head, and Teres Major as supporting muscles. Choose a manageable resistance, move with control, and prioritize consistent technique over speed or load.

Begin the repetition: gradually lower the dumbbells towards your chest, maintaining your elbows at a 90-degree angle.
Complete the repetition: press the dumbbells back up to the setup position, fully extending your arms without locking your elbows.
Continue with control: lower your hips back to the bench, returning to the setup position, and repeat the process for your planned repetitions.
tp: Setup: Adjust the dumbbell and your stance so you can begin Dumbbell Bridge Bench Press from a stable, comfortable position.
Control: Keep the motion smooth and let the intended muscles do the work; reduce the resistance if you need momentum to finish a repetition.
Range and alignment: Use only the range you can control while keeping the working joints aligned. Stop if you feel sharp pain or unusual joint discomfort.
Breathing: Exhale during the effort, inhale during the easier phase, and avoid holding your breath for the entire repetition.

st: Set up for the movement: shift your weight to your right leg and bend your right knee, lowering your body while keeping your left leg straight until your right thigh is parallel to the floor.
Begin the repetition: make sure your right knee is aligned with your foot and your left foot is firmly on the ground with toes pointing upwards.
Complete the repetition: push through your right heel to rise back up to the setup position.
Continue with control: repeat the same movement on your left side to complete one rep. Continue alternating sides for the planned repetitions.
